newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - Feb 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - Feb 28.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Feb. 28:

WASHINGTON - The saga of Terrence Johnson, convicted as a teenage cop killer and released from prison as a promising college graduate, ended on his 34th birthday when he killed himself following a failed bank robbery.
WASHINGTON - Deaths from AIDS in the United States last year fell significantly for the first time since the AIDS epidemic began in the early 1980s.

RICHMOND - Gov. George Allen said that Virginia will help enforce new federal tobacco regulations after all, reversing a potentially embarrassing position statement made the day before by the state's attorney general.
WASHINGTON - Record high temperatures in Washington left the frigid, blizzard-filled winter of 1996 a distant memory.

WASHINGTON - The FBI is investigating whether representatives of China attempted to buy influence among members of Congress through illegal campaign contributions and payments from Chinese-controlled businesses.

WASHINGTON - A dozen senior hospital administrators in the Department of Veterans Affairs have been demoted or pressured to leave their jobs after being accused of sexually harassing female employees or mismanaging their facilities
